Article Title: How Harsh fought through pain to script CWG history, now targets Asiad medal
Article Text:
How judoka Harsh overcame pain

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Harsh Singh's right knee still swells. It still hurts. Every time the Indian judoka steps onto the mat, he is reminded of the ACL and meniscus tear that nearly derailed his career. But at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, pain took a back seat as the 23-year-old scripted history by becoming India's first-ever men's judo gold medallist."The pain never really goes away," Singh told TOI in an interview on Thursday. "Sometimes my knee still swells up and feels tight. During the CWG, I felt the pain and the knee occasionally got swollen. After surgery, the joint never became exactly the way it was before. There's always a little discomfort during fights. You have to ignore it and continue. The medal kept me going."The historic triumph came less than a year after Singh tore his ACL and meniscus while training at the Inspire Institute of Sport (IIS) in Aug 2025. Surgery followed in Oct last in Bengaluru before a year-long rehabilitation helped him return to competition."I was in rehabilitation for almost a year. The entire coaching team at the IIS, recovery specialists and Spencer sir (Mackay, S&C expert) helped me throughout.They rebuilt my strength step by step. Because of the IIS and their entire team, I was able to come back on the mat, qualify for the CWG and represent India," he said.The comeback demanded another battle off the mat. Months away from competition saw his weight rise to nearly 72kg, forcing him to shed more than 12kg to return to his 60kg category. Gold at a ranking tournament and bronze at the senior National championships sealed his place in India's CWG squad.Despite lingering discomfort, Singh dominated in Glasgow, with only a hard-fought semifinal stretching him before he clinched the historic title."The semifinal (against the Australian Pedro Carlos) was the toughest. In the 60kg category, even a small point can decide the match. We didn't want to concede anything and stayed aggressive," he recalled.With CWG gold secured, Singh has already shifted his attention to next year's Asian Games. Training stints in Japan and South Korea are part of his preparations as he looks to bridge the gap with Asia's best."I want to improve my speed, grip and strength. Japanese and Korean players are very fast, so training there will help," he said.Born into a modest family, with his father working as a daily-wage labourer, Singh once trained without owning a judo uniform. Support from the govt's schemes and a privately funded athletes' training centre changed the course of his career."My life has changed because of this medal. More people have started noticing judo," he said. "But the best compliment came from my family. They told me, 'You have made the entire family proud.' That meant more than anything else."Having conquered injury to create CWG history, Singh's next aim is clear — turning a gritty comeback into an Asian Games podium finish.
Article Summary: Harsh Singh became India's first-ever men's judo gold medallist. The 23-year-old tore his ACL and meniscus while training at the Inspire Institute of Sport. Surgery followed in Oct last in Bengaluru before a year-long rehabilitation helped him return to competition.

Article Title: 'I worked tirelessly while staying in Pakistan': Arshad Nadeem blames Glasgow cold for CWG poor show

Arshad Nadeem (AFP Photo)

Pakistan’s Olympic javelin champion Arshad Nadeem has blamed the cold Glasgow weather for his disappointing performance at the Commonwealth Games. The defending champion finished ninth after failing to make the final three rounds, saying the low temperature made his body stiff and affected his usually smooth run-up.Nadeem managed 77.41 metres with his second throw after opening with a foul. His third attempt was 75.39m, leaving him outside the top eight.“The weather was extremely cold and I personally felt that it affected my body. As you have seen in many of my previous competitions, my run-up is usually very smooth, but this time it wasn’t… because my body had become stiff due to the cold conditions. My fitness was good and my health was fine, but ultimately whatever Allah wills is what happens,” he told reporters on Wednesday.Despite the result, Nadeem said he remains determined to make a strong comeback and urged fans to continue supporting him.“Please don’t lose heart and don’t stop supporting me either. Whatever I have achieved has only been possible because Allah blessed me with the opportunity to do it. The respect and recognition Pakistan has received around the world have come through years of hard work. I worked tirelessly while staying in Pakistan,” he added.“God willing, I will prepare with full dedication for the upcoming competitions and once again raise Pakistan’s flag on the international stage.”Nadeem also responded to criticism on social media, saying he understood the disappointment among Pakistani fans.“I have heard many things on social media, but I want everyone to remember that I am Pakistan’s son, and I always will be,” he maintained.Nadeem’s next challenge will be the Lausanne Diamond League in Switzerland on August 21. He will face a strong field that includes India’s Neeraj Chopra , Commonwealth champion Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage, Keshorn Walcott, Anderson Peters and Thomas Rohler.Nadeem will hope to regain his form before the Asian Games later this year.

Article Title: Reality check after Commonwealth Games 2026: India’s boxing renaissance to face ultimate Asian exam
Article Text:
New Delhi, Aug 04 (ANI): Union Minister Kiren Rijiju in a group photograph with Indian boxing contingent (@KirenRijiju X/ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India’s record-breaking boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games has generated plenty of optimism, but the celebrations will quickly give way to a far sterner test when attention shifts to the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from Sept 19 to Oct 4. After returning from Glasgow with a historic haul of seven gold and three silver medals, India’s boxers now head into what many within the sport regard as the closest thing to the Olympics.The CWG triumph underlined the country’s growing depth, particularly in women’s boxing. Sakshi Chaudhary (51kg), Preeti Pawar (54kg), Jaismine Lamboria (57kg), Priya Ghanghas (60kg) and Arundhati Choudhary (70kg) struck gold, while Sachin Siwach (60kg) and Ankush Panghal (80kg) topped the podium in the men’s competition. Olympic medallist Lovlina Borgohain, Jadumani Singh and Narender Berwal added silver medals.The challenge in Aichi-Nagoya, however, will be on an entirely different scale. Unlike the Commonwealth Games, the Asian Games will feature continental powerhouses such as Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, China, Chinese Taipei, Japan and North Korea — nations that have consistently dominated the World Championships and the Olympics.Uzbek stars Mirazizbek Mirzakhalilov and Bobo-Usmon Baturov, along with Kazakhstan’s Kairat Yeraliyev and Ablaikhan Zhussupov, are expected to headline a field packed with world-class talent.India will also be without two of its Commonwealth champions. Jaismine (57kg) and Arundhati (70kg) will miss out because their weight categories do not feature in the Asian Games programme, depriving the country of two genuine medal prospects.“The Asian Games for us is like the Olympics,” Boxing Federation of India president Ajay Singh said. “The best teams in the world today are Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and India, and all three are in Asia. Add a strong Chinese contingent and you understand why it is much tougher. You can’t replicate this (CWG) performance at the Asian Games. But if you win a sizeable number of medals at the Asian Games, you can be hopeful of winning medals at the Olympics too.Women’s head coach Santiago Nieva shared a similar assessment while insisting the team remains on the right path.“We can’t guarantee that we will win gold all the time, but we are on the right track. We know how strong the field will be at the Asian Games. The boxers are aware that they can’t sit on their success,” he said.India had returned with one silver and three bronze medals from the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou. The Glasgow CWG showcased the strides the boxing contingent has made. But it’ll be Aichi-Nagoya that is going to reveal whether the progress is enough to challenge Asia’s finest and signal genuine medal potential for the 2028 Olympics.
Article Summary: India's record-breaking boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games has generated plenty of optimism. But the celebrations will quickly give way to a far sterner test when attention shifts to the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from Sept 19 to Oct 4. India’s boxers now head into what many within the sport regard as the closest thing to the Olympics.

Article Title: Pakistan boxer Qudratullah ‘goes missing’ in Glasgow after Commonwealth Games campaign

Pakistani boxer Qudratullah has reportedly gone missing in Glasgow, just hours before the country’s Commonwealth Games contingent was scheduled to leave for home.According to a report by Pakistani outlet Geo News, sources in the Pakistan Boxing Federation said Qudratullah was last seen in his hotel room at around 2am. Officials later checked his room and found that he was no longer there.The Pakistan team was due to gather in the hotel lobby at 9am before leaving for Pakistan. However, Qudratullah could not be found when officials checked his room, sources said.His passport and return ticket are reportedly still with the team manager. The incident is not the first such case involving a Pakistani boxer abroad, with another promising boxer, Zohaib, reportedly going missing during an international tour of Italy last year.Pakistan’s 21-member contingent finished the 2026 Commonwealth Games with only one medal. Boxer Fatima Zahra won bronze in the women’s 60kg category, giving Pakistan its only podium finish at the Games.The result was Pakistan’s lowest medal tally since the 1998 Commonwealth Games, when the country won one silver. Pakistan had also returned without a medal from the 1990 edition, making Glasgow its poorest CWG campaign in 36 years.Fatima made history by becoming the first Pakistani female boxer to win a Commonwealth Games medal and was later chosen to carry the national flag at the closing ceremony.Pakistan’s biggest medal hope, Olympic javelin champion Arshad Nadeem, also failed to finish on the podium after serving as the country’s flagbearer at the opening ceremony.

Article Title: ‘Like preparing for IIT and UPSC together’: Father Murali shares Sreeshankar’s comeback story
Article Text:
Murali Sreeshankar

KOCHI: S Murali gave an unusual analogy to describe the struggles his son, long jumper Sreeshankar Murali, undertook to regain full fitness after a career-threatening knee injury he sustained two years ago.“Sreeshankar’s comeback was as difficult as preparing for the IIT and Civil Services simultaneously,” he told TOI.Murali is currently near Prague, where he is closely monitoring his son’s training ahead of a busy stretch that begins with the World Athletics Continental Tour (silver level) meet in Bhubaneswar on Aug 22, followed by next month’s Asian Games in Japan.“Sreeshankar’s training now revolves around strength and conditioning, along with the prehab and rehab programme designed by coach Wayne Lombard. There is very little time to work on technique. The priority is to protect the knee on his take-off leg,” Murali said.His IIT-UPSC analogy aptly captures the magnitude of the challenge Sreeshankar faced after suffering the devastating injury just months before the 2024 Paris Olympics.Two years later, the journey came full circle when the 27-year-old clinched the silver medal at last week’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.“Of all the medals Sreeshankar has won, this one gives me the greatest satisfaction because of the circumstances under which he achieved it. It reflects his mental toughness and hunger,” Murali said.The conditions in Glasgow were anything but favourable.“It was around 12 degrees Celsius with drizzle and strong winds, making the runway tricky,” Murali said. Despite the difficult conditions, Sreeshankar produced a best jump of 8.09m to finish second.The performance inevitably brought back painful memories of 2024, when the family received a grim diagnosis after Sreeshankar tore the patellar tendon in his take-off leg.“The doctors in Mumbai had not seen an injury like this. I thought he would never be able to walk again,” Murali recalled.“They told us it wasn’t a common sports injury but the kind usually seen after a serious car accident. His knee was completely ruptured.”Determined to find the best treatment, Murali travelled nearly 1,900 miles with his son to Doha’s Aspetar Hospital. “The surgeons reconstructed his knee using four screws.”The Palakkad athlete spent more than eight months away from competition before beginning the long rehabilitation process.The painstaking recovery paid rich dividends. Since returning to elite competition, Sreeshankar has consistently cleared the eight-metre mark, including a season’s best of 8.38m at the Inter-State Championships in Bhubaneswar in June.“There is no time to bask in the Commonwealth Games glory,” Murali said, pointing to the demanding schedule ahead.Sreeshankar will now turn his attention to the Asian Games in Japan, where he hopes to upgrade the silver medal he won at the previous edition in Hangzhou.“With everything Sreeshankar has gone through, he has every reason to believe he can stand on top of the podium at the Asian Games,” Murali concluded.
Article Summary: Sreeshankar Murali suffered a career-threatening knee injury two years ago. The Palakkad athlete spent more than eight months away from competition before beginning the long rehabilitation process. The 27-year-old clinched the silver medal at last week's Commonwealth Games.

Article Title: 'Nightmare!' Ronaldo suffers his worst Al-Nassr defeat to date as AFC Champions League Elite comeback ends in 4-0 humiliation
Article Text:
Ronaldo and Al-Nassr suffer a shocking 4-0 defeat on their long-awaited AFC Champions League Elite return/ Image: X

Al-Nassr suffer nightmare start against Al-Ain

Ronaldo suffers heaviest Al-Nassr defeat

Al-Nassr have seven matches to repair the damage

Al-Nassr fans turn on Ronaldo and Postecoglou

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Al-Nassr's return to the AFC Champions League Elite was supposed to offer an early glimpse of what the new season could bring. Instead, Cristiano Ronaldo and his teammates walked away from their opening night with a result that few inside the club would have expected, as Ange Postecoglou's side suffered a heavy defeat in the United Arab Emirates.Cristiano Ronaldo started for Al-Nassr, but there was little the captain could do to prevent a disastrous evening as Al-Ain swept aside the Saudi side 4-0 in their first AFC Champions League Elite match of the campaign.The defeat came in Matchday 1 of the newly formatted competition, meaning Al-Nassr's Asian campaign has barely begun, but the manner of the loss immediately puts Postecoglou's team under pressure.Al-Ain took control in the 25th minute, when Houssine Rahimi opened the scoring. Al-Nassr were unable to find a response before Rahimi struck again in the 63rd minute, leaving the visitors with a huge task just to get back into the match.Instead, the collapse continued.Soufiane Rahimi added a third in the 72nd minute, before Georgios Giakoumakis completed the rout five minutes from full-time to seal a stunning 4-0 victory for the UAE side.For all of Al-Nassr's possession, there was remarkably little attacking threat to show for it. Postecoglou's team controlled 58 per cent of possession and won the corner count 10-2, yet managed only three shots on target.Al-Ain, by comparison, registered seven shots on target and made their opportunities count.The result also extends an impressive start to the season for Al-Ain, who arrived unbeaten in their first five UAE Pro League matches, having recorded four wins and one draw.For Ronaldo, the scale of the defeat makes it particularly difficult to dismiss as an ordinary bad night.It is now the heaviest defeat of his Al-Nassr career since he joined the Saudi club in January 2023. His previous worst results in Saudi colours had both ended in three-goal defeats, with Al-Nassr losing 3-0 to Al-Hilal in the Saudi Pro League in December 2023 and 4-1 to the same opponents in the Saudi Super Cup in August 2024.The 4-0 defeat to Al-Ain is therefore a new low in terms of the margin of defeat during Ronaldo's time in Saudi Arabia It does not, however, match the heaviest losses of his entire career. Ronaldo's two worst defeats by goal difference remain Manchester United's 5-0 loss to Liverpool in October 2021 and Real Madrid's 5-0 defeat to Barcelona in November 2010, both five-goal margins.What makes Tuesday's result particularly damaging is when it arrived.Al-Nassr had only just returned to the AFC Champions League Elite after a one-year gap, with a new coach, a new season and renewed expectations surrounding a squad built to compete for major honours.The opening match was supposed to begin that campaign.Instead, Al-Nassr now sit at the bottom of the tournament standings after one match, having conceded four goals without scoring.The new AFC Champions League Elite format gives Al-Nassr some room to recover because this is no longer a traditional four-team group containing six matches.Instead, the competition now features a single league stage in which each team plays eight matches against eight different opponents.That means Al-Nassr have seven matchdays remaining, giving Ronaldo and his teammates plenty of opportunities to climb the table after their disastrous opening.Their next opportunity comes on October 12, when Al-Nassr host FK Neftchi Fergana.The scale of the response will matter as much as the result itself. A one-year absence from the competition had created anticipation around Al-Nassr's return, while Postecoglou had arrived with the task of turning a squad containing Ronaldo and other high-profile additions into a side capable of making a serious continental run.Instead, the first night exposed just how far there is still to go.The reaction from the stands was predictably furious after Al-Nassr were beaten at the Hazza bin Zayed Stadium.Supporters had expected something very different from the club's return to Asia's elite competition, particularly with Ronaldo leading the side and Postecoglou now in charge.Some fans directed their anger towards Ronaldo himself, with the captain's performance described by supporters as “pitiful” amid Al-Nassr's failure to seriously threaten Al-Ain for long periods.Postecoglou faced even sharper criticism.Supporters questioned whether the Australian had made the difference they expected after his appointment, with Al-Nassr appearing short of answers at both ends of the pitch as the scoreline continued to worsen.Calls for his dismissal grew louder as the defeat unfolded.For a club that entered its AFC Champions League Elite return with ambitions of going deep into the competition, there could hardly have been a more damaging opening night. Ronaldo and Al-Nassr now have seven matches to change the story, but the first one has already left them with a four-goal deficit and very little margin for another collapse.
Article Summary: Al-Nassr lost 4-0 to Al-Ain in their first AFC Champions League Elite match. The result leaves the Saudi side bottom of the group after one match. Al-NASSr have seven matches remaining to try and make up for the loss.

Article Title: Real Madrid reportedly ready to do what they did for Ronaldo to ensure Kylian Mbappé win the 2026 Ballon d’Or
Article Text:
Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe celebrates scoring his side's 4th goal during the Spanish La Liga soccer match between Real Madrid and Rayo Vallecano in Madrid, Spain, Saturday, Sept. 12, 2026. (AP Photo/Manu Fernandez)

Real Madrid have a plan for Mbappé's Ballon d'Or bid

Mbappé faces Kane and Yamal in a closely fought race

How the Ballon d'Or voting works

France Football

France Football

L'Équipe

Madrid hope history can repeat itself

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Kylian Mbappé's Ballon d'Or campaign is already gathering momentum, but there is another force working behind the scenes. Real Madrid have been here before, and the club appears ready to revisit a strategy that helped Cristiano Ronaldo win the award despite strong competition from Bayern Munich.Madrid are reportedly preparing to put their full institutional weight behind Mbappé in the weeks leading up to the Ballon d’Or ceremony. The club is expected to call on some of its biggest former stars and most influential figures to publicly highlight the Frenchman’s case, keeping his individual achievements at the centre of the conversation as voting draws closer.According to L’Équipe , this kind of coordinated backing has been part of Madrid’s approach in previous Ballon d’Or campaigns. The club has previously relied on respected figures from its history to champion its leading candidate, using their reputations and influence to reinforce the argument being made on the pitch.Madrid employed a similar strategy in 2013, when Alfredo Di Stéfano, Emilio Butragueño, Carlo Ancelotti, Iker Casillas and Sergio Ramos all publicly backed Cristiano Ronaldo as he competed with Bayern Munich duo Franck Ribéry and Arjen Robben.Ronaldo ultimately won the award, despite not lifting a major team trophy that year. He collected 27.99 per cent of the vote, finishing ahead of Lionel Messi on 24.72 per cent and Ribéry on 23.36 per cent.Ribéry had entered the race after helping Bayern win the Champions League, Bundesliga and German Cup, but Madrid's campaign placed greater emphasis on Ronaldo's individual achievements.Bayern's position was also complicated by the presence of Robben as another candidate from the club, meaning Ribéry did not receive the same unified backing that Ronaldo enjoyed from Madrid.The club now reportedly believes there is value in using the same approach for Mbappé.The challenge for Mbappé is that his competition is particularly strong this year.Harry Kane is currently the bookmakers' favourite, with Lamine Yamal ahead of Mbappé in some of the latest odds, leaving the Real Madrid forward in third despite an outstanding individual campaign.Kane has perhaps the strongest statistical case of the three. No player scored more club goals during the 2025-26 season, with the Bayern Munich striker finding the net 61 times as his side won both the league title and German Cup.Mbappé's case, meanwhile, rests heavily on his own production and his standing as one of the world's most influential forwards.What makes his case especially strong, despite missing out on major silverware, is his complete individual dominance across every major competition. He finished the season as the top scorer in La Liga, the Champions League, and the World Cup, racking up an astonishing 58 goals and 13 assists in 61 matches for club and country.Most notably, he captured the 2026 World Cup Golden Boot with 10 goals, a feat that simultaneously crowned him as the all-time leading scorer in World Cup history with 22 career goals.Madrid cannot manufacture a Ballon d'Or-winning season for their star, and the final decision will still come down to the journalists casting their votes. What the club can do is make sure Mbappé's achievements remain impossible to overlook during the final weeks of the campaign.The Ballon d'Or is awarded annually byto the player judged to have been the best in the world over a single full season.The process begins with a 30-player shortlist, created byand. One journalist from each of the top 100 FIFA-ranked nations then votes for their top 10 players.Points are awarded according to each journalist's ranking, with voters asked to consider three principal factors.Individual performances during the previous season come first, followed by the player's team performances and achievements at both club and international level. Fair play is the third consideration, with the winner also expected to represent the sport positively as an ambassador.Once voting closes, the points are added together and the players are ranked by their totals. If two players finish level on points, the player with the greater number of first-place votes wins.The club's reported strategy is therefore less about changing the voting system than about making sure its preferred candidate remains at the centre of the conversation.When former Madrid greats repeatedly argue that Mbappé deserves the award, their voices carry the weight of the club's history as well as their own reputations within football.That was the thinking behind the Ronaldo campaign in 2013, when Madrid figures collectively pushed his individual case despite the strength of Bayern's trophy haul.The circumstances are different this time, with Kane's goal-scoring record and Yamal's emergence giving voters two compelling alternatives. Yamal's strongest argument is his World Cup triumph, while domestically, he anchored Barcelona as they successfully defended their La Liga title and won the Spanish Super Cup. He was also officially named La Liga Player of the Season. Mbappé will ultimately have to make the strongest case through his performances, and the journalists will decide whether that case is enough.Madrid, however, appear unwilling to leave the result entirely to chance.
Article Summary: Real Madrid have a plan for Kylian Mbappé's Ballon d'Or bid. The club is expected to call on some of its biggest former stars and most influential figures to publicly highlight the Frenchman’s case. Madrid employed a similar strategy in 2013 when Cristiano Ronaldo won the award despite not winning a major team trophy.

The decision involved two of Spain's biggest clubs, a manager he already knew well, and a conversation with José Mourinho that could easily have pulled things in another direction. Months later, the Barcelona midfielder has now explained what ultimately made up his mind.The 30-year-old's decision to leave Manchester City during the summer came as a surprise to some, particularly because Real Madrid had also pursued him. Barcelona eventually secured his signature in a reported £65.4 million move, bringing an end to seven years in England.Rodri has now explained his thinking in an interview with Spanish outlet Mundo Deportivo , making clear that the choice came down primarily to what he believed was best for his career on the pitch.“The first thing I have to say is that I would have liked it to have been a quiet two or three weeks of vacation, but it wasn't like that at all,” Rodri said.“There were many things to consider and such an important decision had to be made with two of the best clubs in the world. In the end, I made my decision based on sporting reasons, on what motivated me the most and on understanding where I could win and grow the most as a player.“It wasn't an easy decision at all; saying no to Real Madrid isn't easy, especially since they treated me exceptionally well. In the end, Deco and Hansi's leadership convinced me.”Rodri expanded on the thinking behind the move, pointing to both Barcelona's current squad and Hansi Flick's plans for the team.“I've always based my decisions on sporting merit, on where I believe I'll be able to win, be happy, and, above all, grow as a player. And that's why I chose Barça, also because of the generation of players they have and what Hansi is able to build.”The move has already begun to look encouraging. Rodri has featured five times since arriving in Catalonia, while Barcelona have made a perfect start to the season, winning all six of their opening matches across five LaLiga games and one Champions League fixture and scoring 26 goals.Barcelona have won back-to-back LaLiga titles and are now hoping Rodri's experience can help them make another step in Europe as they attempt to end an 11-year wait for the Champions League.Rodri also arrives with considerable experience of winning at the highest level. He won the 2026 FIFA World Cup with Spain in July and was awarded the Golden Ball as the tournament's best player.Real Madrid's interest was serious enough for Rodri to have a conversation with Mourinho before making his final decision.The Spain international said the Portuguese coach had “clearly expressed his desire” for him to join Madrid, although Rodri chose not to disclose the private details of their conversation.“I don't think it's appropriate to reveal a private conversation, but he clearly expressed his desire for me to come and what I could contribute to the team,” the Barcelona midfielder said.The conversation did not end badly when Rodri chose Barcelona. Instead, he said he contacted Mourinho himself to thank him for the way Madrid had handled the pursuit.“The interaction was very good. When I made my decision, I also called him to thank him for his interest and the way he treated me. I think he's a fantastic coach; I've shown him my worth wherever he's been during his successful periods, and Real Madrid is going to be a tough rival in this league.”Rodri's role at Barcelona is not simply expected to involve controlling games from midfield. He believes his experience can also help a relatively young squad deal with situations that many of its players have yet to encounter.“I can contribute in different areas,” Rodri said. “If we're talking about experience and leadership, I think I can add a lot to a group of players that is quite young and maybe haven't faced certain situations as much as I have.“And from a footballing perspective, I am here to adapt to the team. It is already a team that works well, we have seen that they're winners already, and I want to add to that and play to my strengths.”Flick has already made clear what he expects from Rodri, with the midfielder recalling one of the first messages he received from his new manager.“One of the first things Hansi told me was about having a desire to improve day by day, to be non-conformist, to never relax, to never believe you've reached your limit and to always demand more.“That is what will lead you to success sooner or later. I believe that Barça have that room for improvement to achieve the kind of excellence that can lead to winning major European titles, having already done so in Spain.”Barcelona return to action against Racing Santander on Wednesday, September 16, with Rodri now preparing for the next stage of a decision that was ultimately made on sporting grounds rather than sentiment.
Article Summary: Rodri reveals why he chose Barcelona, rejecting Real Madrid, and opens up about his private call with Mourinho. The Barcelona midfielder has now explained what ultimately made up his mind. The 30-year-old's decision to leave Manchester City came as a surprise to some, particularly because Real Madrid had also pursued him.

Raheem Sterling has pleaded guilty to dangerous driving

Sterling's football career had already taken a sharp turn

Sterling still has options if he avoids a lengthy absence

Raheem Sterling is facing another uncertain chapter after appearing in court over a May motorway crash. The former England winger was convicted of dangerous driving at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court on Tuesday, leaving him facing the possibility of a significant punishment. His football career was already at a crossroads after being released by Feyenoord following a short and underwhelming spell in the Netherlands. Now, another difficult decision awaits.Sterling appeared at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court on Tuesday, September 15, where he pleaded guilty to dangerous driving following a single-vehicle crash in May.The 31-year-old was charged last month with dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen.The charges relate to an incident on May 28, 2026, when Sterling was driving a Lamborghini Urus on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road before crashing into motorway barriers.Hampshire & Isle of Wight Constabulary said at the time that the collision happened on the M3 southbound near the Minley Interchange.“No other vehicles were involved, and no injuries were reported,” a force spokesperson said in a statement issued to SPORTbible.Sterling has now been convicted of dangerous driving, leaving him facing the possibility of up to two years in prison.The outcome comes at an especially difficult point in a career that once appeared destined to remain among English football's elite.Sterling's conviction arrives after several years in which his career has moved a long way from the heights he reached at Manchester City.The winger joined City from Liverpool in 2015 and became one of Pep Guardiola's most important players, winning the Premier League four times during his spell at the club.His move to Chelsea in 2022 was supposed to mark another major chapter, but his time at Stamford Bridge became increasingly difficult.Sterling made 81 appearances for Chelsea and spent part of the 2024/25 season on loan at Arsenal. By then, he was surplus to requirements in west London and was reportedly banned from using the club's facilities while in exile.His Chelsea contract was eventually terminated by mutual consent in January 2026.Sterling then signed a short-term deal with Feyenoord, where he reunited with former Manchester United and Feyenoord manager Robin van Persie. The move did not last beyond the season, however, after Sterling made just eight appearances in all competitions, playing a total of 481 minutes.Feyenoord opted not to extend his stay into the 2026/27 campaign, leaving the former England international without a club.The court case therefore arrives at a point when Sterling was already trying to work out where his football career could go next.Sterling's conviction does not necessarily mean he will serve time in prison, with the maximum sentence for dangerous driving standing at two years.If he avoids a custodial sentence, his attention is likely to return to finding his next club.At 31, Sterling still has years ahead of him and remains a former 82-cap England international. He scored 20 goals and provided 19 assists for his country, representing England at three World Cups and two European Championships, including their run to the Euro 2020 final. However, his recent form and lack of regular football have made his next move difficult to predict.There was already one potential route outside England before Tuesday's court appearance.Former Liverpool, Swansea City and Newcastle midfielder, now manager of Dubai-based, recently revealed that the club had received enquiries from high-profile free agents.Arabian Falcons compete in the UAE Second Division League, the second tier of UAE football, and Shelvey is trying to guide them towards promotion.When asked by talkSPORT whether players including Sterling and former Manchester United wingerhad shown interest, Shelvey said:“There are a couple that have got in touch.“I don't really deal with that side of it. I am trying to manage the team because I want to get promoted this year.“But it is a fantastic opportunity for people if that is what they are looking for at this stage of their career, or if they are struggling to get a club.“Once the UK window shuts, you are scrambling for clubs, so we put out a call to see if there was anyone who was interested.”Sterling could now consider a move to Dubai with Arabian Falcons or wait to see whether another club in England is prepared to give him an opportunity.The UAE option would represent a significant change from the level at which Sterling spent most of his career, but it would at least give him a route back onto the pitch after his difficult spell at Feyenoord.For a player who once became a central figure in Guardiola's Manchester City side and one of England's most recognisable attackers, the immediate question is no longer where Sterling can reach his peak.It is where he goes from here.

The 31-year-old was charged last month with dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen. The charges relate to an incident on May 28, 2026, when Sterling was driving a Lamborghini Urus on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road.
